t: Section 2(c) of Public Law 96–324 is amended by striking the words “the Canal Zone,”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment striking the words "the Canal Zone," from an existing law. It establishes no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.

opus.w: This section only removes the words "the Canal Zone," from an earlier law. It does not set up any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue for parties outside the federal government. Reading participation into it from the wider context of the amended law is not supported by the text itself.
opus.b: The section is a technical amendment: it strikes the words "the Canal Zone," from Section 2(c) of Public Law 96–324. One might be tempted to read it as part of a larger program that could involve outside parties. But on its face, the section has no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple textual amendment to an existing statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, or coordination with outside parties. It merely directs the removal of specific words from the legal text.
qwen_chat.s: Section 2(c) of Public Law 96–324 is amended by striking the words “the Canal Zone,”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending a law regarding the Canal Zone involves public participation if the Canal Zone had local governance structures. However, the text itself is merely a textual amendment ("striking the words") and does not describe any process of consultation, hearing, or input from outside parties. It is a legislative directive to change the text of a statute, not a procedural requirement for public involvement in a decision.
